newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Wella delights with strong 96 data.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Wella delights with strong 96 data.

text.p: German haircare group Wella AG on Tuesday forecast significantly higher profits and stronger sales this year after sales climbed 10 percent in the first quarter and 1996 results were strong.

"Net profits should climb by 25 percent while sales should grow by seven percent in 1997. We want to grow two to four percent more strongly than the market," Wella management board chairman Joerg von Craushaar told a news conference.
Last year group net profit rose 7.7 percent to 78 million marks ($45.8 million) while sales jumped 8.8 percent to 3.8 billion marks, proving 1995's 41 percent slump in profits had been digested.
Dividends were held steady for the second consecutive year however, with Wella paying 14 marks per preference share and 13 marks per ordinary share.

Return on sales slipped to 2.0 percent last year from 1995's 2.1 percent, but von Craushaar promised a dramatic increase to four percent in the year 2000. "To reach that, our profits have to grow by 25 percent every year," he said.
For 1997, Wella's chief financial officer Hans Schmidt forecast a small rise in the return on sales, to 2.2 percent.
Von Craushaar said a combination of more cost-cuttings, new product launches and an improved distribution network would help propell growth this year.

After suffering the negative consequences of the strong mark in 1995 and the group's rapid expansion, von Craushaar said the currency problems had been largely digested and that problem markets like Russia and Great Britain had swung to profit last year.

Striving to "make Wella into the world's best-know haircare group", von Craushaar said Wella's salon business would grow by six percent while the retail business would grow by seven percent in 1997. He said hair colorants were seen contributing significantly to sales in this area.
Sales in the group's third core business area, perfume and personal care products, should climb by 10 percent, outpacing market growth by some seven percent, von Craushaar said.

Overall, analysts were pleased with Wella's upbeat outlook and last year's stronger than expected results, saying the group had clearly implemented its new strategy and should be able to make good on its ambitious forecasts.
"By saying they want to post disproportionately strong growth, Wella is set to gain market share and that is very positive," said Thomas Deser, analyst at BHF Bank in Frankfurt.
Wella, whose key competitor is French group L'Oreal, received particularly high marks for successfully grabbing market share from lower priced brands like German group Henkel's Schwarzkopf products.

Investors sent preference shares up 14 marks during bourse trade but at the close the stock ended flat at 955 marks as profit-taking hit, sending the broader market down 0.22 percent to 3,340.33 points.

In the fragrance business, where Wella strives to improve its ranking from number eight to one of world's top five, the group launched the new perfume Envy, made by Gucci, with great fanfare in March.
After spending some 35 million marks on the launch, Wella hopes to see sales of at least 75 million marks this year.

"The concept 'envy' is known all over the world, and the perfume has been an absolute hit in Asia and the U.S. since it launch. 'Envy' will move us one step closer to becoming one of the top perfume producers," Edda Wendig, head of the perfume unit said.

Wella acquired the license for Gucci perfumes with its purchase of the French Muelhens group. Looking ahead, von Craushaar said Wella would look selectively for takeovers in the perfume division. "We are not actively looking, but it something were offered to us, we might be tempted."
